facts.statement: Tuojiangosaurus fossils were found in the Upper Shaximiao Formation in Sichuan Province, China.
facts.quote: recovered from the Upper Shaximiao Formation of what is now Sichuan Province in China.

facts.statement: Tuojiangosaurus was a herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic Period.
facts.quote: herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Period

facts.statement: Tuojiangosaurus grew to a length of 6.5 to 7 meters and weighed approximately 2.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: reaching 6.5-7 m in length and 2.8 MT in body mass

facts.statement: The arrangement of tail spikes in Tuojiangosaurus is affectionately known as the "thagomizer".
facts.quote: In stegosauridae, this spike arrangement has become affectionately known as the "thagomizer"

facts.statement: Tuojiangosaurus had at least twenty-five teeth in its lower jaw.
facts.quote: There are at least twenty-five dentary teeth

facts.statement: The teeth of Tuojiangosaurus had a thick base with a cingulum merging into a triangular vertical median ridge.
facts.quote: The teeth have a thick base, cingulum, merging at the inside into a triangular vertical median ridge

facts.statement: Tuojiangosaurus fed on low-lying ground vegetation.
facts.quote: Tuojiangosaurus ate low-lying, ground vegetation

facts.statement: Due to lacking high dorsal spines for muscle insertion found in Stegosaurus, Tuojiangosaurus probably could not stand upright on its hind legs.
facts.quote: Al carecer de las altas espinas dorsales para la inserción de músculos encontrado en las vértebras del Stegosaurus, probablemente no podía alzarse sobre sus piernas traseras

facts.statement: Remains of a stegosaurian were discovered in 1974 during the construction of the Wujiaba dam in Zigong, Sichuan.
facts.quote: In 1974, during construction of the Wujiaba dam in Zigong, Sichuan, the remains of a stegosaurian were found

facts.statement: The species Tuojiangosaurus multispinus was named and described in 1977.
facts.quote: The type and only species of Tuojiangosaurus, Tuojiangosaurus multispinus, was named and described in 1977

facts.statement: Tuojiangosaurus was described by Dong Zhiming, Zhou Shiwu, Li Xuanmin, and Chang Yijong.
facts.quote: by Dong Zhiming, Zhou Shiwu, Li Xuanmin and Chang Yijong

facts.statement: The generic name Tuojiangosaurus is derived from the Tuo River near the holotype's discovery site.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the River (jiāng) Tuo, near which the holotype was found

facts.statement: The specific name multispinus is derived from the Latin words for "many" and "spine".
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Latin multus, "many", and spina, "spine"

facts.statement: Dong originally classified Tuojiangosaurus in the subfamily Stegosaurinae of the family Stegosauridae in 1977.
facts.quote: Tuojiangosaurus was by Dong placed in Stegosauridae in 1977, more precisely in the Stegosaurinae

facts.statement: A 2009 analysis by Mateus, Maidment, and Christiansen found that Tuojiangosaurus fell outside the family Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: An analysis by Octávio Mateus, Maidment, and Nicolai Christiansen, published in 2009, found that Tuojiangosaurus fell outside of Stegosauridae

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis by Raven and Maidment found that Tuojiangosaurus grouped with Huayangosaurus and its relatives.
facts.quote: A more comprehensive analysis by Raven and Maidment in 2017 found that it grouped with Huayangosaurus and its relatives

facts.statement: It is debated whether Tuojiangosaurus is an early or late branching member of Stegosauria, as some analyses place it outside Stegosauridae due to fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: An analysis by Octávio Mateus, Maidment, and Nicolai Christiansen, published in 2009, found that Tuojiangosaurus fell outside of Stegosauridae, though its exact position in Stegosauria (either as an early branching member of the group or a later branching species closer to stegosaurids) was uncertain due to the relatively fragmentary nature of the remains

facts.statement: In 1990, Galton identified a unique trait in Tuojiangosaurus: tail base vertebrae spines possessed bony skirts running from the front to the sides.
facts.quote: In 1990, Peter Malcolm Galton pointed out an autapomorphy: the spines of the vertebrae of the tail base possess spines with bony skirts running from their front to the sides

facts.statement: In 2006, Maidment and Wei identified two additional diagnostic characters: frontal bones wider than long and well-separated ilium processes.
facts.quote: In 2006, Susannah Maidment and Guangbiao Wei would identify two other diagnostic characters: the frontal bones are wider than they are long, and the supraacetabular and posterior processes of the ilium are well-separated

facts.statement: Dong estimated that Tuojiangosaurus had about seventeen pairs of plates and spikes.
facts.quote: Dong estimated there were about seventeen pairs of plates and spikes

facts.statement: Paul interpreted the tail spikes of Tuojiangosaurus as a "pin-cushion array" based on a Chungkingosaurus specimen.
facts.quote: Paul, based on "Chungkingosaurus sp. 3" specimen CV 00208, interpreted the thagomizer as a "pin-cushion array", with two vertical pairs of thick spikes and a third pair of narrow spikes pointing to behind

facts.statement: Tuojiangosaurus lived at the end of the Jurassic Period, approximately 160 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 160 millones de años, en el Oxfordiense

facts.statement: The holotype CV 209 was found in the Upper Shaximiao Formation dating from the Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian stages.
facts.quote: The holotype, CV 209, was found in a layer of the Upper Shaximiao Formation, dating from the Oxfordian-Kimmeridgian

facts.statement: Remains of a stegosaur were discovered in 1974 during the construction of the Wujiaba Dam in Zigong, Sichuan.
facts.quote: En 1974, durante la construcción de la presa de Wujiaba en Zigong, Sichuan, se encontraron los restos de un estegosáurido.

facts.statement: The fossils were recovered from the upper portion of the Shangshaximiao Formation in Sichuan, China.
facts.quote: Recobrado de la porción superior de la Formación Shangshaximiao en la provincia de Sichuan China.

facts.statement: The species Tuojiangosaurus multispinus was named in 1977 by Dong Zhiming, Zhou Shiwu, Li Xuanmin, and Chang Yijong based on two specimens.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y única conocida T. multispinus fue nombrado en 1977, exactamente 100 años después de Stegosaurus, por Othniel Charles Marsh, a partir de dos ejemplares, por Dong Zhiming , Zhou Shiwu , Li Xuanmin y Chang Yijong.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen CV 209 dates to the Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian stages of the Upper Shaximiao Formation.
facts.quote: El holotipo , CV 209, se encontró en una capa de la Formación Superior Shaximiao, que data del Oxfordiense al Kimmeridgiense.

facts.statement: In 1977, the holotype represented the most complete stegosaurian skeleton found in Asia.
facts.quote: En 1977, representó el esqueleto de estegosáurido más completo encontrado en Asia.

facts.statement: Additional material, including juveniles, has been referred to the species since the initial discovery.
facts.quote: Posteriormente, se ha remitido más material, incluidos los juveniles.

facts.statement: A cast of the original fossilized skeleton found in the Wujiaba Quarry in 1977 is exhibited at the Bolton Museum in the UK.
facts.quote: Un molde del esqueleto de dinosaurio fosilizado original, encontrado en Wujiaba Quarry 1977, también está en exhibición en el Museo Bolton , Reino Unido.

facts.statement: Dong classified Tuojiangosaurus in the family Stegosauridae, specifically within the subfamily Stegosaurinae, in 1977.
facts.quote: Tuojiangosaurus fue colocado por Dong en Stegosauridae en 1977, más precisamente en Stegosaurinae.

facts.statement: A 2004 cladistic analysis by Galton placed Tuojiangosaurus in a derived position as the sister species of Chialingosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2004, un análisis cladístico realizado por Galton recuperó a Tuojiangosaurus en una posición bastante derivada, como una especie hermana de Chialingosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2009 analysis by Mateus, Maidment, and Christiansen found that Tuojiangosaurus fell outside Stegosauridae, though its exact position within Stegosauria remained uncertain due to fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: Un análisis de Octávio Mateus, Maidment y Nicolai Christiansen, publicado en 2009, encontró que Tuojiangosaurus cayó fuera de Stegosauridae, aunque su posición exacta en Stegosauria, ya sea como un miembro de ramificación temprana del grupo o una especie de ramificación posterior más cercana a los estegosáuridos, era incierta debido a la naturaleza relativamente fragmentaria de los restos.

facts.statement: A more complete 2017 analysis by Raven and Maidment found that Tuojiangosaurus grouped with Huayangosaurus and its relatives.
facts.quote: Un análisis más completo realizado por Raven y Maidment en 2017 encontró que se agrupaba con Huayangosaurus y sus parientes.

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Tuojiangosaurus is Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Stegosauridae

facts.statement: Tuojiangosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Tuojiangosaurus lived during the Bathonian to Callovian stages, approximately 168.2 to 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Callovian (168.2 to 161.5 million years ago)
